ageing_relevance.rationale: About 10% of B2M papers concern ageing, and it is one of the GrimAge plasma proteins. Open Targets lists no age-related disease associations. The DNAm surrogate was higher in schizophrenia/FEP, but that is a methylation estimate, not measured protein.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up the GrimAge clock. Part 1 of this project: the GrimAge clock as a whole was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia, a difference that disappeared after adjusting for a methylation smoking score; this protein's own surrogate was not tested. Surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Shirai et al. 2024 (7-cohort meta-analysis): this protein's DNAm surrogate was higher in schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis in a model adjusted for age, sex and DNAm smoking pack-years.

background_knowledge: Circulating B2M rises with age and has been reported in rodent studies to impair cognition and neurogenesis (not from the tools).

mechanism.rationale: The core function is well understood: it is the MHC class I light chain and it is secreted. The causal link to ageing and the direction of modulation are not established.

evidence.value: Component of the class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Involved in the presentation of peptide antigens to the immune system. Exogenously applied M.tuberculosis EsxA or EsxA-EsxB (or EsxA expressed in host) binds B2M and decreases its export to the cell surface (total protein levels do not change), probably leading to defects in class I antigen presentation (PubMed:25356553)

background_knowledge: Systemic lowering of circulating B2M might be beneficial, but this is not shown in humans.

tractability.rationale: Open Targets shows small-molecule evidence (structure with ligand, high-quality pocket), antibody and PROTAC evidence. None of it is clinically validated.

safety.rationale: No liabilities are listed, but absence of data is not evidence of safety. B2M is needed for MHC class I, and the top disease association is MHC class I deficiency, so broad inhibition could impair immunity.
background_knowledge: B2M loss abolishes MHC class I surface expression, which affects antigen presentation and immune surveillance.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs are listed for B2M.

assessment.summary: B2M is the secreted MHC class I light chain and one of the GrimAge plasma proteins. About 10% of its literature concerns ageing, but Open Targets lists no age-related disease associations. Its DNAm surrogate was higher in schizophrenia/FEP, which says nothing directly about the measured protein. Tractability evidence exists across several modalities, but there are no clinical candidates and the safety data are empty. The immune role of B2M is a theoretical concern. The direction of modulation is unclear, so my recommendation is consider.
key_uncertainties: Whether lowering circulating B2M slows ageing in humans (causal evidence, e.g. Mendelian randomisation or interventional data)
Whether measured B2M protein, rather than its DNAm surrogate, differs in schizophrenia
Whether selective targeting of circulating B2M would avoid disrupting MHC class I function
No clinical or safety data to define a therapeutic window
source_conflicts: Tractability lists small-molecule, antibody and PROTAC evidence, but the clinical candidates list has no drugs. I relied on the clinical list for precedence and treated tractability as unproven.
The ageing literature share is about 10%, but Open Targets has no ageing disease associations. I treated ageing relevance as moderate.
The safety list is empty, but the top association is MHC class I deficiency, which suggests an on-target immune liability. I scored safety as uncertain (3), not as clean.
